newsitem.title: USA: Argentine bond fits debt management thrust - Kiguel.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bond fits debt management thrust - Kiguel.

text.p: Argentine Undersecretary of Finance Miguel Kiguel said the country's $2 billion 20-year global bond priced Wednesday lengthens the nation's debt maturity, thus easing the strain of short-term debt.

Speaking to Reuters by phone after the pricing of the bond, Kiguel said the new bond, fetching the tightest spread at 462.5 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, is the longest maturity of Argentina's dollar-denominated debt since the Brady bonds.
"We try to avoid concentration (in short-dated debt)," he said.
Kiguel said timing of the issue was opportune as the declining yields of U.S. Treasuries market provided a friendly backdrop.
Looking to future issuance, Kiguel reiterated that Argentina would issue another $1 billion worth of bonds before the end of the first quarter and it is likely to be denominated in German marks.

Although Argentina intends to lengthen the maturity of its debt profile perhaps by issuing 30-year bonds in dollars, Kiquel said the officials are looking "to balance the maturity with (interest rate) cost."
